stories.summary: The former Sakharov Prize laureate ran against Aliaksandr Lukashenka for the Belarusian presidency in 2006.
stories.article_text_excerpt: Aliaksandr Milinkevich, the physicist-turned-politician who united Belarus’s opposition forces to challenge Aliaksandr Lukashenka in the 2006 presidential election, has died at the age of 79.His death was announced on Tuesday.Milinkevich underwent a complicated operation to remove a blood clot from his carotid artery last year. He spent a prolonged period in critical condition and later underwent extensive rehabilitation.From academia to politicsMilinkevich was born in 1947, in Grodno, Belarus. After graduating from the faculty of physics and mathematics at the Grodno Pedagogical Institute, he worked as a teacher at a local school. The symbolic step is part of new Prime Minister Peter Magyar's sweeping efforts to dismantle the legacy of former premier Viktor Orban after winning April's general elections . Baka was a staunch critic of Orban who was removed from his Supreme Court role during the former PM's tenure. stories.article_text_excerpt: Watch: What is it like to travel on Air Force One with Trump? Watch: What is it like to travel on Air Force One with Trump? Close President Donald Trump secretly swapped planes as he left a Nato summit in Turkey last month, according to US media. Footage from 8 July shows him boarding Air Force One, the presidential jet, at Ankara airport. But according to the Washington Post, he was then secretly taken to a smaller C-32A military aircraft - a modified Boeing 757 often used by the vice-president - via a catering truck, which had been elevated to plane level on the opposite side to where he had boarded. Journalists and some White House staff boarded Air Force One and were reportedly told to close their window shades. They were unaware the president was no longer on board. The BBC's State Department correspondent Tom Bateman shares what it's like to be onboard Air Force One with the president as part of the press pool. Read more about the story here . stories.article_text_excerpt: Image source, AFP via Getty Images Image caption, A woman wades through floodwaters outside her inundated house at a village in Assam's Sivasagar By Soutik Biswas India correspondent Published 2 hours ago Well past midnight on 19 July, as floodwaters surged through a village in India's northeastern state of Assam, Bornali Baruah and her husband were trying to save his 97-year-old mother. Almost bedridden, Lokada Duarah could not walk. There was no boat, no rescue team and no neighbour available to help. So they lifted her onto a makeshift raft made of banana trunks, and carried her through the rushing water towards safety. "Everyone was trying to save themselves," Baruah says. An hour later, she says, the three of them reached a shelter camp on a national highway some distance away from their house in Charing village in Sivasagar district, one of the worst flood-affected districts. The water was three to four feet deep and the current so strong that they had to move slowly, holding each other's hands and using sticks to steady themselves. In all, more than 4,380 infections have been recorded. The current outbreak is the 17th ever recorded in the DRC, with Sania Nishtar of the Gavi global vaccine alliance warning it could become "the largest outbreak ever." Until now, the worst outbreak recorded in the DRC was the one that took place from 2018 to 2020 when some 3,500 infections led to 2,300 deaths. The pace of death is gathering momentum this time around, with the virus spreading faster and exhibiting a higher mortality rate than the 2014-2016 West African outbreak — the worst outbreak on record, which logged 28,000 infections and more than 11,000 deaths. By Samantha Granville Beirut Published 3 hours ago Lebanon's parliament has voted to abolish the death penalty, a move that would make it the first country in the Middle East to formally end capital punishment. A majority of MPs in the 128-seat parliament backed the measure on Tuesday, while Hezbollah's parliamentary bloc voted against it. The legislation will now go to the cabinet before being passed to President Joseph Aoun for signing. The government has already expressed its support for the measure. Lebanon has not carried out an execution since January 2004, although courts have continued to hand down death sentences. Rights groups estimate that more than 78 people remain on death row. Under the new legislation, capital punishment will be replaced with life imprisonment with hard labour. However, the legislation does not yet set out in detail how the new sentence would be enforced. stories.article_text_excerpt: Victorian parliament has voted to abolish group voting tickets (GVTs) to elect its upper house. The state was the only remaining jurisdiction with the system, in which voters can only choose one party above the line on the ballot paper, with their preferences then allocated by the party if it’s knocked out during counting. GVTs have been criticised by experts including Antony Green because they allowed backroom deals between parties to flourish, enabling some candidates to get elected with only a minuscule number of primary votes. The electoral amendment (miscellaneous matters) bill 2026, which passed the upper house 33 votes to 4, will replace GVTs with a new above-the-line voting system that requires voters to number at least five groups in order of preference. Those preferences will then flow to candidates in the order they appear below the line for each party or group. stories.title: Study: Obesity 'bigger cancer risk' than previously thought
stories.summary: A new study has found that being significantly overweight could be responsible for more cases of cancer than previously known. Abdominal fat, in particular, increases the risk of cancer — especially among women.

stories.summary: Drought is gripping large parts of Europe, with soils unusually dry and major rivers running low. A strengthening El Nino could push global temperatures even higher later this year.

stories.title: Type 2 diabetes in young women increasingly common
stories.summary: British researchers say rates of type 2 diabetes are growing most among women under 40. The disease is often underdiagnosed in women or diagnosed too late to reverse the condition's progression.
